articles.title: Factory in Bangladesh that "redefines manufacturing architecture" wins RIBA International Prize
articles.summary: A rug factory in Rangpur, Bangladesh, designed by Dhaka-based studio Nakshabid Architects to dismantle workplace hierarchies, has won the RIBA International Prize for 2026. Named Green Field Factory, the project is the fifth winner of the biennial award, presented by the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) to the world's best new building outside the UK. articles.title: HARMAY Changsha Guojin Street Store / STUDIO SPLASH
articles.summary: Located on Guojin Street at the core of Changsha's Wuyi Square commercial district, the project sits within an underground retail spine linking street-level entrances with subterranean transit hubs, marked by crisscrossing interior corridors. The HARMAY store occupies the B1 level, bridging the B2 double-height atrium with the north-south ground access routes at a major intersection of pedestrian circulation.

articles.title: CCLM 280 House / Barbalaco Arquitectos
articles.summary: Located in a residential neighborhood in the Cañuelas district, this weekend home was conceived from the very beginning as a gathering place to share with family and friends.

articles.title: Ella House / Studio Memo
articles.summary: Casa Ella is divided into two blocks around a central garden, connected by a fluid path of ramps that link the zones at every half-level up to a roof garden, gradually revealing the relationships between the home's interior and exterior. It features a sculptural volumetry that embraces, protects, and welcomes, while also enabling multiple connections with the outdoors. Among the design solutions adopted, the project prioritizes the residents' privacy while offering spaces filled with natural light.
